label: copy phase (after the delimiter step)
explanation: Broad copy-phase feature: active on about 92% of copy-phase steps (t > L) and holds essentially 100% of the activation mass there. It is almost never active during the original-token phase (292 steps) or on the <DEL> delimiter step itself (0.4%). Activation rate rises with recall_idx/t (about 0.88-0.98). It shows little dependence on token identity, L, n_digits or first_tok. The largest activations (top examples near the max) are on the first fed-back copy input (recall_idx 1) when that input is g (the first original token being g), and activation then decays over the following copy steps. Inactive copy steps are scattered with no clear pattern. Missed activations are tiny (<0.1% of mass) and occur on <DEL> or the last original token.

issues: Minor overclaim: the explanation says the activation rate 'rises with recall_idx from about 0.88 to 0.98', but the curve is not monotonic. Dev rates by recall_idx 1..8 are 0.909, 0.944, 0.927, 0.878, 0.886, 0.935, 0.968, 0.979, so the rate dips in the middle of the copy phase and rises at the end. By t (copy only) it is similarly uneven. The 0.88-0.98 range is right; the word 'rises' is not.

Some lower-precision subgroups exist, but none is systematic enough to change the predicate. Precision is 0.83 at L=4, recall_idx=1, and 0.73 at L=3, recall_idx=1 (only 13k steps). By out_tok, r is lowest at 0.785 and 3 is 0.83. By in_tok, every token is between 0.87 and 1.0. Repeated inputs (in_tok == prev_tok), digit inputs, in_count >= 2 and the last step (to_go == 0) all sit at 0.90-0.96. The 8% of copy steps where the feature is silent look like scattered near-threshold dips, not a clean class.

Verified claims: 292 active steps in the original phase and 0.4% on the delimiter step. The copy phase holds 100% of the activation mass. Missed activations are on <DEL> and the last original token (orig_idx 7/8) and hold 0.0% of the mass. The predicate (phase==2) & (recall_idx==1) & (in_tok == g) has precision 1.0, and the top examples confirm that the largest activations are on the first fed-back g and decay over the following steps. Test scores reproduce: P 0.919, R 0.999, F1 0.958, mass recall 1.000.
